The Wanin Desert, also known as the Great Ocunese Desert, is an arid region in the southern part of the [[Mahea]] that covers an area of 1,526,074 km2 (948,258 sq mi) mostly located in [[Byllu]], [[Taing]] and [[Ocaun]]. It is the world's seventh-largest desert and the world's fourth-largest cold desert.

About 85% of the Wanin Desert is in [[Ocaun]], and the rest is located in neighbouring countries. The Wanin Desert is about _________ % of the total geographical area of [[Ocaun]]. More than 60% of the desert lies in the Ocunese state of [[Sinachta]]; the portion in Ocaun also extends into the neighbouring provinces. [[The Kasive]] lies to the north of the Wanin desert, the [[Knac Steppe]] lies to its south, and borders the [[Otemvi]] to the west. 

===Geography===
The northeastern part of the Wanin Desert lies between the [[Allscht Hills]]. Much of the desert area is covered by huge, shifting [[wikipedia:Dune|dunes]] that receive sediments from the [[wikipedia:Alluvial_plain|alluvial plains]]. The sand is highly mobile due to the strong winds that rise each year. The [[Koita River]] is the only river that stretches into the desert. Rainfall is 100 to 500 mm (4 to 20 in) per year, almost all of it between June and September.

Tools belonging to the [[Prehistoric Otemvi cultures|prehistoric Otemvi culture]] have been discovered in Middle Palaeolithic deposits in the Wanin Desert.
===Climate===
The climate is a [[wikipedia:Desert_climate#Cold_desert_climates|cold desert]]. The desert receives between 100 and 200 millimetres of precipitation in an average year, with more falling in the northern areas. Average maximum temperatures range from 20 to 26 °C (68.0 to 78.8 °F) in July, and from −12 to −18 °C (10.4 to −0.4 °F) in January. Very high winds sweep across the plains at times

The desert has both a very dry part, and it is surrounded by semidesert parts that have fewer dunes and slightly more precipitation
